Get school attendance zones

Source: R/zones.R
gcd_school_zones.Rd

Attendance-zone polygons: the areas that assign a home to its zoned elementary, middle and high school, one polygon per school, level and grade run, for the current school year.

Zones differ in precision. Some are the district's official GIS layers; others are digitized from PDF maps, rebuilt from street lists, or are the whole district outline (districts with one school per grade). Read method and accuracy_class before treating zones as equally exact, and see gcd_school_zone_coverage() for how completely each district was collected. A zone is the default assignment, not an official enrollment determination: confirm with the district.

A statewide pull is large, especially at resolution = "full". Filter to a district and keep the "display" default for maps.

Usage

gcd_school_zones(
  district_code = NULL,
  school_code = NULL,
  district = NULL,
  school = NULL,
  zone_level = NULL,
  grade = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  resolution = c("display", "full"),
  geometry = TRUE
)

Arguments

district_code, school_code

Character vectors of codes. Default NULL.

district, school

Names, matched to codes as in gcd_rows(). A school name found in more than one district needs district too. Default NULL.

zone_level

"elementary", "middle" and/or "high". Default NULL: all.

grade

One grade: keep zones serving it ("pk", "k", "01" to "12"; "5" and "K" are accepted). Default NULL: all.

year

The zones' school year as its ending year (2027 is 2026-27). Default NULL: the current zones.

resolution

"display" (default): simplified polygons for maps, much smaller; "full": the source polygons the point lookup uses.

geometry

TRUE (default) returns an sf object (needs the 'sf' package); FALSE returns the attributes as a plain tibble.

Value

An sf object (or, with geometry = FALSE, a tibble), one row per zone, with columns year (integer), district_code, district_name, school_code, school_name, zone_level, grade_low, grade_high ("pk", "k", "01" ... "12"), method (how the zone was built), accuracy_class, currency_status, boundary_vintage, source_url, retrieved_on (Date), area_sq_mi, the bounding box (bbox_xmin, bbox_ymin, bbox_xmax, bbox_ymax), source_school_name (the name as the district's map spells it), then positional_rmse_m, currency_note, source_publisher, nces_school_id, district_census_id, nces_lea_id and the geometry (WGS 84). The API's disclaimer is the note attribute.

See also

gcd_locate() to find the zones a point falls in; gcd_school_zone_status() for schools without a zone; gcd_describe() with "school_attendance_zones" for every field.

Other geography: gcd_district_boundaries(), gcd_locate(), gcd_school_zone_coverage(), gcd_school_zone_status()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)
zones <- gcd_school_zones(district = "Atlanta Public Schools",
                          zone_level = "high")
plot(zones["school_name"])

gcd_school_zones(district_code = "630", geometry = FALSE)
}
